chunks.arabic_text: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَيَّارٍ، يَكْنَى أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، الْقُمِّيُّ، الْمَعْرُوفُ بِالسَّيَّارِيِّ. ضَعِيفٌ، مُتَهَالِكٌ، غَالٍ، مُنْحَرِفٌ. اسْتَثْنَى شُيُوخُ الْقُمِّيِّينَ رِوَايَتَهُ مِنْ كِتَابِ "نَوَادِرِ الْحِكْمَةِ". وَحَكَى عَلِيُّ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْهُ فِي كِتَابِ "النَّوَادِرِ" الْمُصَنَّفِ أَنَّهُ قَالَ بِالتَّنَاسُخِ.

translations.en: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sayyar, known by the kunya Abu Abdillah, al-Qummi, known as al-Sayyari. Weak, careless, Ghali, deviated. The Shaykhs of Qum excluded his narrations in the book 'Nawadir al-Hikma'. And Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Mahbub reported about him in the compiled book 'al-Nawadir' that he said with reincarnation.

en.summary: This entry highlights Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Sayyari as a prominent yet controversial figure in Qum, characterized by his 'Ghuluw' (exaggeration in Imamate authority) and deviation, leading the Qum scholars to selectively exclude his narrations from 'Nawadir al-Hikma'. The specific mention of his belief in reincarnation (al-tanasukh) by Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Mahbub underscores the theological diversity and occasional heterodoxy within early Shia circles, distinguishing his views from the mainstream acceptance of bodily resurrection.
en.seo_question: Who was Ahmad ibn Sayyar and what was his status in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.غَالٍ: Ghali (one who exaggerates the virtues of the Imams)
